constraints.note: Frames t0001/t0002 (evid 25-50): EE descends to table level and contacts the block's right side face; contact normal is horizontal, pushing leftward toward the pad. Side contact is required for non-prehensile lateral pushing (top-down contact cannot translate the block), and the contact normal makes this 'side' even with the wrist overhead. Core.

Unscoped during-stage claim contradicted by frames: at t0000-t0002 (frames 0-50) the block center is far right of the pad center; centers only converge at stage end. The true at_end fact is already the acceptance item; as a stage constraint the scope is evidence-contradicted.

Nothing is grasped: t0002-t0004 show the EE pushing with its closed finger/tool face against the block's side; fingers never close around the block and it is never lifted. Non-prehensile task; grasp vocabulary misuse (the extractor's own _comment_ignored admits contact-based pushing).

Derived order s0<s1 is load-bearing: the coarse push delivers the block to the pad but leaves it ~120 deg mis-rotated (t0004), which fine_alignment then corrects (t0008_50). Fine alignment also cannot start from the initial far-right position (t0000); reversing or dropping the order fails.

acceptance.note: holds=at_end contradicted: at s0 end (t0004, frame ~100) the block's long axis is grossly non-parallel to the pad marker (~+120 deg off per pixel measurement; visibly rotated vs the gray T in t0003/t0004). Orientation is only recovered in s1.

t0004: the block has been delivered onto the pad footprint region (coarse center alignment). This is the actual completion condition of the coarse push; without it the fine stage cannot work in contact range.

constraints.note: t0005_12-t0007_38: wrist hangs overhead but the finger/tool contacts the block's side faces at table level (clearest t0007_38, EE beside the block with horizontal contact normal) to nudge/rotate it in plane. The horizontal contact normal makes this 'side'; required for planar fine pushing. Core.

Unscoped during-stage claim contradicted at stage start: s1 begins (t0004/frame 100) with the block ~120 deg mis-aligned, and orientation only converges near the end (t0008_50). The correct at_end version is credited in acceptance; as a stage-scope constraint it is evidence-contradicted.

Maintained coarse center containment during fine rotation is real and load-bearing: the block stays over the pad footprint throughout s1 (on pad at t0004; still there t0007_38, t0008_50; t0005/t0006 partially occluded by EE but position continuity is clear). Rotating the block off the pad would fail the task.

acceptance.note: t0008_50 (frame 212): the gray T marker is completely hidden under the red block - centers coincide within footprint tolerance. Core end condition.

t0008_50: marker fully covered by the block implies matched orientation (~+2 deg residual per pixel measurement). T-block is not rotationally symmetric so this is core - symmetry exemption does not apply.

missing.name: inside
missing.note: Footprint containment is the true acceptance: undirected axis_parallel + center_align are also satisfied by a 180-deg-flipped T (T-block not rotationally symmetric). The demo end state is exactly containment - at t0008_50 the gray marker is completely hidden inside the block footprint. Without inside(), a flipped-T solution passes the extracted acceptance.

constraints.note: Argument misuse: clearance(t_block_red, pad_gray) demands separation between block and pad, but the demo's end state requires them coincident - the block sits exactly on the pad, unchanged across t0008_72-t0009_40. The intended (and visible) constraint is clearance between the retracting ARM/EE and the block; neither arg refers to the arm.

acceptance.note: Same argument misuse as the stage constraint: block-pad clearance at end of cleanup would mean the task failed. Frames t0009_18/t0009_40 show block and pad coincident (marker hidden under block) while the arm is home - the extracted acceptance is contradicted by the successful demo itself.

missing.name: clearance
missing.note: The constraint the extractor mis-argued: the retracting arm must clear the aligned block. Visible in t0008_72-t0009_40 - EE lifts up and away to home while the block pose is pixel-identical across all cleanup frames.

missing.name: center_align
missing.note: Cleanup must leave the achieved state intact: block-pad center alignment has to survive the retract (holds at end of episode). With the extracted clearance args wrong, nothing currently checks the block was not disturbed. Supported: block position unchanged t0008_72 -> t0009_40.

missing.name: axis_parallel
missing.note: Same maintenance requirement for orientation: final ~+2 deg alignment must survive the retract; a nudge during retreat re-rotates the asymmetric T. Supported by unchanged block orientation across cleanup frames.
